Definition: from G2794; to undergo peril:--be in danger, be (stand) in jeopardy.
BiblicalUsage: Kindyneuo means to be in danger, to stand in jeopardy. Luke 8:23 has the disciples in jeopardy on the lake when the storm fills the boat, Acts 19:27 and Acts 19:40 have Demetrius and the town clerk warning that the silversmiths' craft and the city itself are in danger, and 1 Corinthians 15:30 has Paul asking, why stand we in jeopardy every hour?
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Paul's question answers the storm: the disciples were in jeopardy for an hour, and Paul stood in it every hour, because the gospel is worth the danger. I hold that jeopardy is the normal weather of the Christian life, not the exception.
